subject: Voyager Health — post-call hosting synopsis and immediate asks
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Anika Suresh <anika.suresh@voyagerhealth.eu>, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@voyagerhealth.eu>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Voyager Health — post-call hosting synopsis and immediate asks

Hi Anika / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from our side and a list of immediate asks so we can line up a technical deep-dive next week. I focused the notes on the constraints you emphasized on the call; please flag anything missing or off.

Key pain points we heard
- Must keep all patient data resident in the EU (primary requirement).
- For PHI workflows, leadership prefers an air-gapped or highly restricted on-prem/VPC deployment; egress must be strictly controlled and minimal.
- No persistent outbound connections to third-party telemetry endpoints are allowed by policy; occasional signed callbacks are acceptable under whitelist.
- VPN/DirectConnect only; client cannot allow any public NAT egress without explicit justification.
- Backup and retention policies: 7 year retention on audit logs and ability to hand off logs for compliance audit.

Goals voiced by Voyager
- Deploy Redwood Private inside their EU VPC or on-prem colo to serve clinical note generation with sub-300ms median latency for 256-token prompts.
- Validate we can meet SOC2 + local data residency controls and provide artifact evidence for procurement.
- Run a 4-week PoC with a small production workload (50–100 QPS peak) and automated fallbacks to smaller models if capacity constrained.

Technical constraints / questions we agreed to clarify
1) Network topology — you said outbound is locked down; can we get a preliminary network diagram showing allowed egress endpoints, firewall rules, and whether an outbound proxy is acceptable? (see attached checklist)
2) Certificate & key management — do you require HSM-backed keys for model encryption, or is KMS integration sufficient?
3) Ops windows — what are maintenance blackout windows for the clinical environment?
4) Audit artifacts — what specific artifacts (syslogs, terraform state, control plane audit) will procurement need?

Immediate asks (next 3 business days)
- Anika: send the preliminary network diagram and a short list of firewall rules (high level) so our infra team can confirm compatibility.
- Tom: confirm who on your procurement/legal side will receive SOC2 + technical evidence.
- Ben/Marissa: schedule the technical deep-dive (Redwood infra + security) for next Tuesday/Wednesday (I'm proposing Wed 16:00 CET).

Attachments included: redwood-private-network-checklist.pdf (short checklist), voyager-prelim-network-diagram.png (your diagram you sketched on the call).

If all looks good I'll schedule the deep-dive and share a short agenda.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[dylan.brooks@redwood.com] | +1 (415) 555-0149

From: Anika Suresh <anika.suresh@voyagerhealth.eu>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@voyagerhealth.eu>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Voyager Health — post-call hosting synopsis and immediate asks

Thanks Dylan —

Appreciate the clear summary. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- The diagram attached is a preliminary internal sketch (I pulled the PNG back from the call notes). I will have our network team annotate exact firewall ports by EOD Friday.
- For key management: we prefer HSM for signing keys used in audit, but KMS is fine for dataset encryption if the provider supports EU-only key operations.
- Maintenance blackout: no changes between 08:00–18:00 CET on weekdays for the clinical cluster.

Procurement: I'll loop in our procurement lead (TBD) separately; Tom will send the name/contact this afternoon.

We are OK to do Wed 16:00 CET for the technical deep-dive (Tom and our infra lead will join).

Quick note: one regulatory nuance — our compliance officer flagged that backups cannot leave the VPC unless encrypted with customer-managed keys AND only after approval. We'll send the compliance checklist tomorrow.

Best,
Anika

--
Anika Suresh
Head of Platform Engineering, Voyager Health
anika.suresh@voyagerhealth.eu | +44 20 7946 0991

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anika Suresh <anika.suresh@voyagerhealth.eu>, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@voyagerhealth.eu>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 12:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Voyager Health — post-call hosting synopsis and immediate asks

Anika / Tom —

Thanks for the fast replies and the clarifications — helpful. Quick operational notes from our infra side ahead of the deep-dive:

Checklist summary (will cover in detail on Wed)
- Deployment modes we can support: Dedicated EU VPC, Customer VPC peering, or fully air-gapped on-prem (appliance install).
- Egress model options: 1) Zero outbound (control plane via customer proxy), 2) Whitelisted outbound to Redwood control endpoints over TLS via customer NAT, 3) Intermittent signed callbacks via SFTP/HTTPS to customer-approved endpoints.
- Keys: we support HSM (via partner integrations) for signing and CMK for encryption; we can run with customer-managed keys in EU-only KMS.
- Audit artifacts: we can supply syslog streams, structured request/response traces, model versioning history, and signed SHA hashes for model binaries.

I've attached a short network checklist (redwood-private-network-checklist.pdf) to use as a baseline for your network team's annotations. For the deep-dive agenda I've proposed:
1) 10m introductions & PoC goals
2) 25m network/topology walk (you present annotated diagram)
3) 20m security/artifact requirements (audit, retention, key mgmt)
4) 15m PoC sizing & SLA discussion
5) 10m next steps / procurement touchpoints

If the agenda looks good I'll send a calendar invite for Wed 16:00 CET and include a Zoom + a guarded temporary lab account for a quick connectivity smoke test post-call.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0192

From: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@voyagerhealth.eu>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Suresh <anika.suresh@voyagerhealth.eu>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Voyager Health — post-call hosting synopsis and immediate asks

Thanks all —

Agenda looks good to me. Procurement contact: Nicola Meyer (nicola.meyer@voyagerhealth.eu). She will want the SOC2 Type II report and the data residency write-up; I'll copy her on the follow-up invite.

We will annotate the firewall/export rules and send the compliance checklist by EOD Monday. For the deep-dive, please include a short slide that explains your fallback behavior when a model variant becomes unavailable (this matters for our uptime SLA conversation).

See you on Wed.

Tom

--
Tom Reilly
CTO, Voyager Health
tom.reilly@voyagerhealth.eu | +44 20 7946 0992
